task_retrieval_key: A one-day-old male infant, born at term with a birth weight of 3.1 kg, presented with no significant prenatal history and an uncomplicated delivery. Since birth, the infant had not passed stool and exhibited increased bilious vomiting and abdominal swelling. The anus was observed to be in a normal position with well-developed gluteal muscles and skin folds. The genital examination showed normally developed male genitalia with no visible signs of a fistula. The urine was clear and free from meconium contamination. A catheter could not be inserted more than half an inch into the anal opening.

avoid: Do not treat an unsupported agent assertion as clinical evidence
recommended_check: Verify source binding before using the evidence for support or refute
